terms.meaning: A tool that runs an app and its needed parts inside a sealed package called a container.
A tool that starts several containers together from one description file.
A sealed, runnable package holding one part of the app.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Database, cache and backend services
sections.what: Starts the PostgreSQL database with the vector add-on, the Redis helper, and the backend API. It sets their connection details, mounts the code and upload folders, and waits for the database and Redis to pass health checks before starting the backend.
sections.why: The backend cannot work without the database and Redis, so Docker is told to start them first and wait for them.
sections.watch_out: The backend mounts the local code folder, so edits on your computer take effect inside the container immediately.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Background worker and frontend services
sections.what: Starts a background worker that runs queued jobs and a frontend development server on port 3000. The frontend is set to call the API on localhost port 8000.
sections.why: Likely reason: some work, such as long AI tasks, should run outside the web request, and the frontend needs its own server.
sections.watch_out: The worker command points to a module named tasks.celery. Confirm that this module exists before relying on background jobs.

summary: Describes the group of services that run together in Docker: a PostgreSQL database, a Redis helper, the backend API, a background worker and the frontend.
purpose: Starts the whole platform with one command so it runs the same way on any computer.
why: Likely reason: the app depends on several services, and Docker keeps their versions and connections consistent.
how: Docker reads the file, builds the backend and frontend images, starts the database and Redis first, waits until they are healthy, then starts the backend, the background worker and the frontend.
inputs: Values from the environment file, such as the database password and environment name, plus the source folders.
outputs: Running services on local ports: 5432 for the database, 6379 for Redis, 8000 for the API, and 3000 for the frontend.
risks: The database password defaults to a weak development value. The database and Redis ports are open to the whole network. The worker command names a module that is not shown in this project, so it may fail.
debug: Run the status command to see which services are up. Check the logs of a service that stops. If the backend cannot reach the database, check that the host name is postgres inside Docker.
